main_text.head: in einem vnbegreifflichen geheimnus essen vnd trincken.
main_text.p: 9In hoc syllogismo amphibologia est in propositione, falsa assumptio, & plus incommodum in conclusione, quàm sequitur è præmissis. Nec enim 1. ut de conclusione primo loco agitur, si vera est hæc conclusio: oralis manducatio & bibitio indignorum in sacra cœna cum corpore & sanguine Christi est sacra cœna aliquid habet conjunctum, quod agat, (muß etwas zuschaffen haben) Ergò vera propterea est explicatio, hœc indigni Christiani necessariò in sacra cœna Christi corpus & sanguinem mediante pane & vino in incomprehensibili mysterio comedunt & bibunt. Nec enim ex indefinita ea, aliquid, ετwas zuschaffenden: licet definire & determinare argumentum, ergò hoc præcisè, ut manducent & bibant. Paulus enim definivit nobis illud aliquid, quomodo versentur indigni, circa corpus Domini, quando scribit, Qui manducat & bibit indignè, judicium sibi manducat & bibit, non dijudicans Corpus Domini. Videtur ergò quid sit Aliquid illud, quo contrahitur reatus. Non tam manducatio & bibitio ipsa, quàm non dijudicando corpus Domini. Et hinc jam secundo patet paraphibologia propositionis. page.notes: The right-hand column is cut off and only fragments of words are legible, so it is not transcribed. Several words in the first paragraph are smudged and doubtful, e.g. "amphibologia", "conclusione", "conjunctum", "hœc" at the line end; the marginal mark "9" is faint. The German parenthesis is partly illegible. Right-hand column fragment is cut off and largely illegible; the Greek word in the line "ετwas" is a garbled printed word, copied as far as legible. Several words are damaged by stains and are uncertain, notably "mysterio", "ετwas", "paraphibologia" (read as "phibologia" in the scan) and "conse-" at the line end.
